sections.text: The sage who realises the unity of life and who worships Me in all beings, lives in Me, whatever may be his lot.
O Arjuna! He is the perfect saint who, taught by the likeness within himself, sees the same Self everywhere, whether the outer form be pleasurable or painful.
Arjuna said: I do not see how I can attain this state of equanimity which Thou hast revealed, owing to the restlessness of my mind.

We had been discussing chapter six, Dhyana Yoga, Yoga of Meditation. In chapter two, Sankhya Yoga, we learned how to differentiate between the self and non self. Self is that which is Ajaha, which is unborn and imperishable.
Nayanam Chindanti Sastrani Nayanam Dhati Pavaka. That which cannot be destroyed by anything, by weapons or fire or water or air. Thats the definition of the self.
Anything which does not fit into the definition is non self. So everything which I consider myself today does not fit into that definition. I was born, I have a birth date and I may have a death date.
And everything which I know about me and my possessions fall into the same category. So it all falls into non self. So my world is populated by non self only.
All that I consider myself so far as me is also non self. My body has a birth and death. My mind has beginning and end.
My intellect has beginning and end. So everything that I associate myself and considered to be me is non self. So now the search for the self.
How do I find myself? So we have learned up to chapter five how to purify the mind and intellect. In other words, how to prepare yourself for this search for running a marathon. You first have to prepare for it the whole period of training.
So the second chapter onward we had this clear instruction how to prepare your mind. So once that mind is prepared, which we call Yoga Rudha, one who is now prepared to take on this journey for the search of the self. So chapter six we started that journey.
How to find the journey once the mind is prepared. When it becomes sinless, that the word we constantly keep using in every language that you wash your sins. In other words, the mind is cleared of all the impurities.
We learn the mind is nothing but the thought channels. A thought occurs, second thought follows that same thought. Third thought now follows the second thought.
It is now creating a channel. Those channels are created which has become my mind and it is all going outwards. Im thinking about something other than me now the same Mind I have to turn towards me the self.
So everything I have learned so far is about non self. All my education, all my contemplation on what is good and what is bad, all that is about non self. So now I have to turn towards myself, the self.
Thats chapter six, Dhyana Yoga, Yoga of Meditation -- how to prepare yourself and position yourself so that you can start that inward journey. We have seen the clear instruction that once you have prepared your mind and purified it of all the sins, you start this journey of Dhyana Yoga. Constantly doing that search, you will come to a point where you will find that bliss.
From verse 28 onward, it says the yogi is always engaging the mind: Yunjan evam sada atmanam yogi vigata kalmashah -- one who is freed of all sins. In other words all the impurities of the mind. Mind which has tendency to see wrong things or going in a wrong direction that I have now adjusted the mind focuses on the right thing, clearly sees this is non self and searching for the Self that Sukena Brahma sans Parsam.
Very easily it enjoys the contact with the Brahman. He easily can understand what the Self is. So clear goal here is to do inward search about what is the self is all about.
When do I consider that my search has yield some results? The next one is Sarva Bhuta Stamatmanam Sarva Bhutani Chaatmani. When I start seeing that self which Im searching as the real self, not the non self is not only residing in me, but residing in all beings searching for myself. In tone I found the eternal self which is residing all beings and Sarva Bhutani Ch Aatmani and I see the all beings are in the Self.
My standard example, all the houses, all the buildings, I see the space. But then I also see that all the buildings are in the space because the space is all pervading. I was searching for the space for my own room once I realized the nature of the self.
I realized that space is the same in all the buildings in the world. And all the buildings are nothing but in that all pervading self. Once that awareness takes place, then I realize I am now truly understand what the nature of the space is.
Space is not something which I create as an architect, not something I can buy from Lowes or Home Depot. I can only buy material to condition my space. Space is universal and all pervading.
Once that understanding takes place about the self Bhagavan said he will say sarvatra samadharsanaha. Now he can see the equality everywhere. Now he sees the connectivity everywhere.
Yomam pashyati sarvatra sarvam chamay pashati tasya ahamna pranasyami sachamena pranashati. So here comes basically an assurance. Is it something that one time I understand in meditation that I have suddenly and then next day I go to work and I forget all about it? Once you have that understanding of all pervading self, that connection with yourself will never get broken, will never be separated.
Once I understood the nature of the space, the space is all pervading. These are all conditioning. The buildings we create, the things which are in the space, then my understanding of the space will never go away, no matter what Im doing.
Yomam pashyati sarvatya. The one who sees me everywhere, Sarvamchyamay pashyati. All the being, all the things, he sees me in it.
Now, every time Krishna uses the word me, hes referring to this supreme self. The big I is what he is referring to. The conditioned I is the small I, as we call it, and the big I is the unconditioned I. So when Krishna says me, hes referring to the unconditioned I, which is all-pervading.
Yoma M. Pasade sir, one who sees me in all things and all things in me. Because now there is no differentiation between the self and the non self.
Even the non self was nothing but the part of this. If something is all pervading, there is no space left for anything else to exist. Its only Im limited.
There is a space for other people. If I buy all the real estate in Richmond, can you buy anything else? No, theres no nothing left for you to buy. Its only when I leave out a parcel and say I dont want that, then you can come and buy.
That when I have recognized myself is all pervading, there is nothing left for anything else to exist. But now I have a vision now of the equality in this plurality. So yomam pasyati sarvatra sarvam chamayi pasyati tasya ahamna pranayami.
For him I never get separated. Once that vision takes place, you are never separated from it. Once I wake up from my dream, I never get separated from the waker.
Both dreamer and waker are now connected to the waker. Dreamer also remembers that I am the waker I was dreamer, now I am a waker. Same dreamer is now waker.
The waker knows I am the waker who was dreaming. Having woken up, I dont go back to the dreaming state. Once Im established in my waking state, I never get separated from it till I go to sleep again. Similarly, once that understanding takes place that myself is nothing but the all-pervading self, I never get separated from myself.
The verse says sa cha me na pranashyati -- and now comes the assurance from the all-pervading Lord: I will never get separated from him. That relationship is dual relationship. I have relationship with him and he has relationship with me.
It is not a one-sided love. If I liked her, but she never knew I exist -- I say, I will never leave you, but she says, I dont even know that you exist. I, the conditioned self has now recognized that Im nothing but the manifestation of the me of the supreme self. The supreme self knows that I am not conditioned in this body mind.
So this relationship is mutual relationship. Both exist in their own perspective. The supreme self exists from a perspective of the macrocosm.
And my conditioned self exists in a perspective of the microcosm. The room space exists as a. We can be meeting here on Sunday morning.
If I say room space does not exist, only universal space exists. Go and meet in a Louis Ginter garden same as meeting here. No, we have to come here.
This is where we meet. It does exist, but it is nothing but the manifestation of this supreme space. In the same way, my conditioned self exists as an ego identifying with this conditioning.
But it clearly knows that this is purely an identification with conditioning, for the convenience of transacting with other conditioned selves. So the next verse says: Sarva bhuta sthitam yo mam bhajati ekatvam asthitah. Once weve established ourselves in this unity, having seen what the self truly is -- my search was to understand: if this body is my non-self, this mind is my non-self, this intellect is my non-self, then what is myself? I found that the consciousness which is not conditioned by this body, mind, and intellect is myself.
Thats why in meditation the whole goal is to not be aware of your body, not be aware of your thoughts or your intellect. Because intellect can become a hindrance in understanding. The more I consider that Im pretty smart, the more I do dumb things.
The more I give up my idea about my intellectual superiority, the more I learn about myself. So Bhagavan said, the one who is Ekatvam asthitah -- the one who is now established in the unity of all things -- has realized that my conditioning and your conditioning are very different. You are not me and I am not you.
You have your own limitations, I have mine. But the essence which makes me who I am, and the essence of who you are, is one and the same. The self in you and self in I is one and the same.
That unity I have found. We constantly search commonness. We come across a new person.
We dont try to find how different we are from each other. First thing we try to find what is common among us. I say, I am from Richmond.
Oh, I am also from Richmond. Okay, we have one commonness we found. Then we gradually say, okay.
Where do you come from? Well, I come from Surat. Oh, Im also from Surat. More we find commonness, more we feel comfort.
Then we are not worried as much about the differences which we have. The differences drop more common things. We find the people whom we love, all the negative things about them.
We dont pay attention to our children, our grandchildren. They are mischievous, laugh it off. We feel good about it.
We say, how cute it is. Somebody else do that to you. Because we found something common.
So the first search for every human being or every being is to find commonness among ourselves. Once we find more things common, more identification occurs. First in the college I saw her.
Then I found out she takes the same chemistry class I do common. Then I found out she comes from the same town I come from. More things I found common, more I identify with her.

Verse 32 offers a profound standard: Atmaupamyena sarvatra samam pashyati - one who sees equality everywhere through the analogy of the self is the supreme yogi. What is this analogy? I know that I want happiness and freedom from suffering. Through self-examination, I recognize that this same desire motivates every other being. Thus I understand others by understanding myself. This becomes the basis for true compassion: I would never do to others what I would not want done to me, and I naturally wish for others what I wish for myself.
Then comes Arjunas honest doubt in verse 33, which mirrors the doubt of every sincere seeker: I do not see how this yoga of equanimity can be maintained, owing to the restlessness of my mind. This is not a lack of faith but clear-eyed self-assessment. Arjuna has listened to all the teachings about steady minds and seeing sameness everywhere, and his experience tells him: my mind is not like that. It constantly chases finer things - Marriott over Super 8, not Seven-Eleven coffee once a better brand is discovered. How can such a mind ever become stable?
The beauty of this passage is that Arjuna voices what we feel but may be too embarrassed to admit. His honesty opens the door for Krishnas practical response. Today, be equally honest with yourself. Where do you find the teachings beautiful but impractical? What specific aspect of your restless mind seems most untameable? Write it down. Naming the obstacle is the first step toward addressing it. Remember, Arjuna is not rejected for his doubt - he is answered with understanding and solutions.
